easy.q: When Elder Morgan was a young teenager getting ready for school, who read the Book of Mormon out loud to him every day?
options: His grandfather
His mother
His seminary teacher
easy.why: Elder Morgan said his mother read to him from the Book of Mormon every day, out loud, “whether I was listening or not.”

easy.q: What lesson did Elder Morgan say he learned from those daily readings?
options: Reading the Book of Mormon helps only if we listen closely
Reading the Book of Mormon is best saved for Sundays
No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon
easy.why: He remembered very little of the words, yet he taught, “No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon.”

easy.q: Elder Morgan wondered aloud why he had been so interested in religion as a boy. What did his wife, Rebecca, say it was?
options: Covenants
Curiosity
Friendships
easy.why: Rebecca said, “I know what it was! It was covenants.” His ancestors had made covenants in the temple in Nauvoo.

easy.q: Elder Morgan compared covenants with God to a great power that stretches across the universe. Which power was it?
options: Starlight
Electricity
Gravity
easy.why: He said that like the binding power of gravity, “covenants with God stretch over all time and all space.”

easy.q: As he closed his talk, what did Elder Morgan tell us about our own story and our family's story?
options: It was all settled a long time ago
It is not all written; don't ever give up
It is ours alone to write and to finish
easy.why: Elder Morgan testified, “Your story, your family’s story, is not all written,” and that God is the author and finisher of it.

medium.q: Elder Morgan borrowed Joseph Smith's words, “I knew it, and I knew that God knew it, and I could not deny it.” What was he describing?
options: His mother's feelings about the Book of Mormon
The testimony he had been given that this is the Lord's Church
His ancestors' choice to stay behind in Nauvoo
Rebecca's sudden insight about covenants
medium.why: After two months of sincere seeking he came to know this is the Lord's Church. Though he would face questions from his family, he said he “had been given a gift—a testimony.”

medium.q: In the prophetic teaching Rebecca read to Elder Morgan, what is promised about “sheep” who wander?
options: The promises made to their parents are withdrawn
They are safe where they are and need never return
The Shepherd notices them once they turn back
The Shepherd's eye is on them and they will feel drawn back
medium.why: The teaching says that “though some of the sheep may wander, the eye of the Shepherd is upon them,” and they will feel Divine Providence drawing them back to the fold.

medium.q: What did Elder Morgan mean when he said covenants with God are “generational in their impact”?
options: They bless not just the person who makes them but those who come after
They bless a family for one generation and then come to an end
They grow weaker with each generation that passes
They matter most to the oldest generation in a family
medium.why: He taught that covenants “do not bless just the maker of the covenant,” and that we are all the intended beneficiaries of countless covenants.

medium.q: How did Elder Morgan connect the Atonement of Jesus Christ to his message about covenants?
options: It ended the need for covenants made by earlier generations
It reaches only those who have already made covenants
It fulfills the greatest promise God made, and its reach is infinite
It is a separate gift that works apart from God's promises
medium.why: He said the Atonement is the fulfillment of “the greatest promise God made,” that Jesus Christ would be our Savior, and that the reach of that covenant is infinite and eternal.

medium.q: What did Elder Morgan counsel those who are crying out to God because a child is struggling?
options: Expect an answer right away if their faith is strong enough
Keep their covenants, cheerfully do what they can, and trust God's timing
Keep working until they have solved the problem themselves
Set the worry aside, since the outcome is out of their hands
medium.why: He said God hears and will answer “in His own time and in His own way,” and invited us to keep our covenants, strive to be faithful, and then stand still with assurance.

hard.q: Which statement best matches what Elder Morgan taught about parents' covenants and their children's choices?
options: Faithful parents' covenants override the choices their children make
Parents' covenants bless the parents but leave their posterity untouched
Parents' covenants help only children who have made covenants too
Parents' covenants leave children's agency intact yet truly affect posterity
hard.why: He drew a careful line: covenant faithfulness “does not alter the agency of children or grandchildren,” yet there is a discernible impact on all our posterity.

hard.q: Elder Morgan concluded that his ancestors’ temple covenants had affected him as a boy seeking truth. How did he say that influence worked?
options: The power of God in those covenants reached out after him
Learning his ancestors’ story stirred him to seek the truth
Their covenants counted as his own until he could be baptized
Their covenants settled in advance which church he would join
hard.why: He said, “The power of God in those covenants reached out after me.” The covenants were theirs, not his, and the power in them was God’s; his agency remained his own.

hard.q: A father reads the Book of Mormon to his restless children each morning and wonders if it matters. Which part of Elder Morgan's story speaks most directly to him?
options: He attended two congregations for two months while seeking truth
His ancestors were baptized by Oliver Cowdery in 1831
He recalled only two phrases, yet knew his mother knew it was true
His wife read him prophetic teachings about sealings
hard.why: More than any words he heard, Elder Morgan knew the Book of Mormon mattered to his mother: “And I knew she knew it was true.”

hard.q: How did the Lord's covenant with Enos support Elder Morgan's teaching that there is no limit to the power of God in our covenants?
options: Enos saw the covenant fulfilled during his own lifetime
Later prophets had to renew the covenant to keep it alive
The covenant was kept as soon as the people repented
The covenant held even though it took over 2,000 years to fulfill
hard.why: He asked whether that covenant had a time limit, then answered that it “would take more than 2,000 years to be fulfilled.” Time does not weaken God's promises.

hard.q: At 14, when he began to question the church of his childhood, what did Elder Morgan already know and what was he still unsure about?
options: He knew which church was true but doubted the Book of Mormon
He knew the Book of Mormon was true but was unsure where the true Church was
He knew Joseph Smith was a prophet but had never heard the Book of Mormon
He knew little about the Restoration and was unsure about all of it
hard.why: Because of his mother he knew the Book of Mormon was true and Joseph Smith was a prophet, yet he was “confused and uncertain” as to where the true Church of Jesus Christ was.
